summary: Tulku Hungkar Dorje studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Tulku Sherdor studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, learning under Ted Norton, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Tulku Thondup studied at Dodrupchen Monastery under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche. He later served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

A Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche studied under Samten Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Karsé Kongtrul, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He founded Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.
Working in linguistics and history and archaeology, Tuomo Pekkanen studied under Pentti Aalto and held a post at the University of Jyväskylä from circa 1972 to 1998.

Working in Tibetology, linguistics, and sinology, Turrell V. Wylie earned his B.A. from the University of Washington and studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima. He served as an associate professor (1958) and professor (1970) at Washington.
Tutob Chökyi Wangchuk studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Trulshik Rinpoche.
Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Tyler Dewar studied at the Nitartha Institute and under traditional teachers Tashi Wangchuk, Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, and Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche.
Working in Indology and linguistics, Tyler M. Richard held a post in South Asian Studies at Harvard University and served on the faculty at the University of Texas at Austin.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Tzungkuen Wen completed a PhD at the University of Queensland under Primož Pecenko, Tamara Ditrich, and Chris Kang. He taught at Fuyan Buddhist Institute and headed a center at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Working in Indology and linguistics, U-tain Wongsathit earned a Ph.D. in Sanskrit from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 2010 and held a post at Silpakorn University in 2003.

Working in Indology and philosophy, U. Ghimire earned degrees including a PhD from Nepal Sanskrit University. Professional posts include Rambadevi College of Medical Sciences (2012-2015), Global Health Alliance Nepal (2015-2016), and the Government of Nepal (2017).
An Indologist, U. V. Swaminatha Iyer held academic posts at Pachaiyappa's College from circa 1903 to 1919 and at Annamalai University from circa 1932 to 1935.

Linguist Udaya Narayana Singh earned degrees from Calcutta and Delhi universities. He held posts at MS University of Baroda, South Gujarat, Delhi, Hyderabad, Visva-Bharati, Amity University Gurugram, and served as Director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages (2000-2009).

A scholar in Tibetology and linguistics, Udo Posch completed his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna under Herbert W. Duda and Robert Bleichsteiner. He later held posts at the University of Graz (1952) and the University of Washington (1953).
Working in Tibetology and history and archaeology, Ugyen Pelgen earned a master's degree from Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, Ujjwal Kumar earned a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University, where he was an assistant professor (2006-2016) before becoming a professor at the University of Calcutta in 2016.

Working in Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology, Ulrich Mammitzsch studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Hamburg, SIU Carbondale, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (Ph.D.). He served as director of East Asian Studies at Western Washington University in 1971.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Ulrich Pagel studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme. In 1999, he was appointed Seiyi Kiriyama Professor in Buddhist Studies at SOAS University of London.

Ulrich Schneider, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig under Friedrich Weller. He held posts at Leipzig, the University of Freiburg (1959-1980), and the University of Münster (1980-1987).
